rationale: This quasi-experimental impact evaluation uses propensity score matching (PSM), hurdle models, and instrumental-variable regressions to assess two Indonesian central-to-local intergovernmental performance grant pilots (DAK Reimbursement/P2D2 and Water Hibah). The sole focal legal/governance mechanism is intergovernmental fiscal allocation rules (`institutional_structure_coordination`), specifically output-based performance grants from the Ministry of Finance to local governments (kabupaten and kota). Empirically, the study co-equally evaluates institutional/fiscal intermediate outcomes (`administrative_outcome`: local government capital spending in Tables 3-4 and local government equity investments in municipal water utilities/PDAMs in Tables 5-7) alongside physical household water network hookups (`primary_connection`: log of new household water connections per 1,000 people in Tables 8-10), making `primary_connection` the primary WASH access outcome family and `multiple` the overall outcome label.
